title: Geometric fibre defects in regular surface point blowups
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$, residue field $k$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Fix a uniformizer $\pi\in R$. Let $T\to S$ be flat and of finite type [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $T$ regular of pure dimension two [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. For a closed point $x\in T_k$, put $l=\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. The blowup $q:T^+\to T$ of the reduced point $x$ [def-nagata-global-blowup] is regular and has exceptional curve $E\cong\mathbf P^1_l$ [def-sc-p1-standard]. Its coefficient in the divisor of $\pi$ is $d=\max\{r:\pi\in\mathfrak m_x^r\}$. Strict transforms of fibre components retain their coefficients and function fields. A component with coefficient greater than one stays nonreduced in the scheme-theoretic fibre. An exceptional $\mathbf P^1_l$ for finite inseparable $l/k$ stays non-geometrically-reduced under strict transform. Every later point blowup with centre on a component of coefficient greater than one creates another component of coefficient greater than one. Every later point blowup centred on the strict transform of an exceptional $\mathbf P^1_l$ with $l/k$ inseparable has centre residue field containing $l$ and again creates a non-geometrically-reduced exceptional curve. If $T\to S$ has nodal geometric fibres near $x$, a centre at a nonsmooth fibre point has $d=2$. A centre at a smooth fibre point with $l/k$ separable has $d=1$ and the blowup remains nodal near $E$. The morphism $q$ has nonempty geometrically connected fibres (also without the nodality or separability assumptions). A smooth centre with $l/k$ inseparable instead creates a non-geometrically-reduced exceptional component. A nodal geometric fibre here is reduced of pure dimension one, and each nonsmooth closed point has completed local ring $\Omega[[x,y]]/(xy)$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The intermediate geometric fibres need not be connected. The map $q$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], $T^+\to S$ is flat and finitely presented, and if $T\to S$ is projective then $T^+\to S$ is projective [def-kun-projective].

source.place: Agent fibre-divisor calculation from Tag 0AGQ (lemma-blowup), using the regular-parameter charts A[y/x] and A[x/y]; models.tex Tag 0CDC (example-blowup), including n=1, and Tag 0CDD (lemma-etale-local-at-worst-nodal). Inseparability persistence uses the inclusion of l in residue fields of points of P^1_l; no perfectness is assumed.

proof.text: First reduce to the integral component containing the centre. The finite-type Noetherian theorem makes $T$ Noetherian. A regular local ring is a domain, so distinct irreducible components cannot meet; there are finitely many components, hence each is open and closed. Each is integral and has dimension two. The DVR is universally catenary by the regular-ring catenarity theorem. For a component meeting the special fibre put $r=\operatorname{trdeg}_K K(T_i)$. The dimension formula gives height at most $1+r$ at every point, and height exactly $1+r$ at a closed special-fibre point: its residue field is finite over $k$ by Zariski's lemma. Such a point exists since the special fibre is nonempty and finite type over $k$. Thus $\dim T_i=1+r$, so $r=1$. In particular $l/k$ is finite and $A=\mathcal O_{T,x}$ is regular local of dimension two. Flatness makes $\pi$ a nonzerodivisor, in particular a nonzero element of its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$.

Blowup commutes with localization, since localization is flat. Apply the local surface blowup geometry to $A$: above $x$ the blowup is regular and its scheme-theoretic fibre is the effective Cartier curve $E=\mathbf P^1_l$. Away from $x$ it is an isomorphism. These two statements prove regularity of $T^+$ everywhere. The properness theorem for a finite-type centre applies because the reduced point ideal is locally finitely generated on the Noetherian scheme $T$. In particular $q$ is proper and of finite type. No excellence or perfectness hypothesis enters. The same holds at every stage of a sequence of point blowups centred at closed special-fibre points, by induction on the number of blowups: each $T_j$ is regular and finite type over $S$, and every closed special-fibre point $y$ of $T_{j+1}$ has $\mathcal O_{T_{j+1},y}$ regular local of dimension two, by the closed-point clause of the local surface theorem when $y$ lies on the new exceptional curve and by the complement isomorphism otherwise. Hence step 1's conclusion about the local ring at the centre, which is all that this step and step 3 use, holds at every later centre.

Choose parameters $a,b$ of $A$. They form a regular sequence in both orders. Krull intersection gives $\bigcap_n\mathfrak m^n=0$; thus $\pi\ne0$ has finite order $d\ge1$. The regular-sequence graded theorem identifies $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}A$ with $l[\bar a,\bar b]$. Write $\pi=\sum_{i=0}^d c_i a^{d-i}b^i$. Its initial form $F(X,Y)=\sum_i\bar c_iX^{d-i}Y^i$ is nonzero, since otherwise this expression would belong to $\mathfrak m^{d+1}$. On the $a$-chart $C=A[\mathfrak m/a]=A[t]/(at-b)$ we have $\pi=a^dG$ with $G=\sum_i c_it^i$. Reduction modulo $a$ gives $C/(a)=l[t]$ and $\bar G=F(1,t)\ne0$. Therefore $G$ is a unit at the generic point $(a)$ of $E$. This local ring is a DVR with uniformizer $a$: it is regular and its maximal ideal is generated by $a$. Consequently the coefficient of $E$ in $\operatorname{div}(\pi)$ is exactly $d$. The $b$-chart gives the same value on the overlap.

proof.text: For an irreducible component $D$ of the special fibre, its generic point is different from the closed centre. The complement isomorphism and the definition of strict transform identify an open neighbourhood of this generic point with its inverse image. They therefore identify its function field and its local ring in the total surface, carrying $\pi$ to $\pi$. The coefficient (the valuation of $\pi$ in that local DVR) is unchanged. The same reasoning applies at each stage of a sequence of point blowups.

source.place: Tag 080E (lemma-strict-transform), restriction over the complement of the centre.

proof.text: At a component generic point with coefficient $m>1$, write $\pi=u z^m$ in its DVR, where $u$ is a unit. In the special-fibre local ring $A_{(z)}/(\pi)$, the image of $z$ is nonzero and nilpotent, so the fibre remains nonreduced there. Now let $y$ be a later closed centre on this component. The regular local UFD theorem gives in $B=\mathcal O_{T_j,y}$ a prime equation $h$ for the component, and a factorization $\pi=h^m v$ with $v\in B$ (the exponent agrees with the generic valuation). Since $h\in\mathfrak m_y$, we have $\pi\in\mathfrak m_y^m$. Step 3 applied at $y$ shows that the new exceptional coefficient is at least $m>1$. This proves both assertions about multiplicity defects by induction on the number of later blowups.

source.place: Tag 0AG0 (lemma-regular-local-UFD), together with the explicit order calculation in step 3.

proof.text: Suppose an exceptional curve is $D=\mathbf P^1_l$ with finite inseparable $l/k$. By the inseparable-element and tensor-nilpotent lemmas, $l\otimes_k\bar k$ has a nonzero nilpotent. This remains nonzero on the affine chart $(l\otimes_k\bar k)[t]$, so $D$ is not geometrically reduced. More precisely it remains nonzero in $l(t)\otimes_k\bar k$: the injection $l\hookrightarrow l(t)$ stays injective after tensoring with the $k$-vector space $\bar k$ (extend a basis). Thus the defect occurs at the component's generic point, and the function-field invariance of step 4 already shows that it survives any strict transform.

source.place: Tags 030V and 030W (lemma-characterize-separable-field-extensions), with the polynomial and rational-function extension calculation.

proof.text: In fact each later strict transform of this $D$ is isomorphic to $D$. If the centre lies off $D$, this follows from the complement isomorphism. If it lies on $D$, the strict transform is the blowup of $D$ in that reduced point. Its ideal is invertible: on a standard affine chart $l[t]$ the point ideal is generated by its irreducible polynomial; near infinity use the other chart. These equations are nonzerodivisors, and away from the point the ideal is the unit ideal. The blowup of an invertible ideal is the identity. Thus every point $y$ on the transformed $D$ has a residue-field inclusion $l\hookrightarrow\kappa(y)$. For closed $y$, $\kappa(y)/k$ is finite by Zariski's lemma and is inseparable since it contains an inseparable element of $l$. The new exceptional curve is $\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(y)}$ by step 2; step 6 proves it again non-geometrically-reduced. This gives the asserted persistence through arbitrarily many later point blowups.

source.place: Tag 080E (lemma-strict-transform), identification with the blowup on D, and the invertible-ideal case; algebra.tex Tag 030W for inseparability.

proof.text:
Record the local comparison used in the next step. For an etale local map $A\to B$ at chosen points, the discrete reduced fibre gives $\mathfrak m_AB=\mathfrak m_B$; flatness gives
$$ (\mathfrak m_A^r/\mathfrak m_A^{r+1})\otimes_{\kappa(A)}\kappa(B)\cong\mathfrak m_B^r/\mathfrak m_B^{r+1}. $$
Tensoring a nonzero vector with a field extension does not kill it. Thus orders agree, as do dimensions of cotangent spaces. The etale local-dimension theorem gives $\dim A=\dim B$, so the definition of regularity shows that one local ring is regular exactly when the other is. A trait uniformizer also remains a uniformizer up to a unit: its ideal extends to the maximal ideal and the new local dimension is one. These arguments apply to both maps in a common pointed etale neighbourhood.

source.place: Morphisms Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field); more-algebra.tex Tags 07QP (lemma-dimension-etale-extension) and 0AH0 (lemma-regular-etale-extension), whose proof is precisely the maximal-ideal and cotangent-space comparison written here.

proof.text: Assume the geometric fibres are nodal near $x$ and $x$ is a nonsmooth fibre point. Apply the nodal-family etale local model. After a pointed etale extension of the trait and of $T$, the equation is $uv-h$ over an etale DVR $R'$. The node is $u=v=\pi'=0$. The possibilities are $h=0$ or $h=\epsilon(\pi')^n$, $n\ge1$; absorb the unit in one variable. The first possibility has zero divisors at the node and cannot be regular. In the second, the nodal-chart regularity criterion says that the total local ring is regular exactly when $n=1$. Hence the regular case is $uv=\pi'$ and $\pi'$ has order two: $(u,v)$ is a regular parameter system, and its associated graded is the polynomial ring with the nonzero degree-two monomial $\bar u\bar v$. By step 8 the uniformizer order is unchanged through these local etale maps, so $d=2$ in the original local ring, and step 3 gives exceptional coefficient two.

source.place: Tag 0CDD (lemma-etale-local-at-worst-nodal) and Tag 0CDC (example-blowup), regular n=1 case; curves.tex Tag 0CBY (lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family).

proof.text: At a smooth fibre point, the flat-fibre smoothness criterion makes $T\to S$ smooth near $x$: it is flat by hypothesis and locally of finite presentation since it is finite type over the Noetherian DVR. The smooth-fibre regularity theorem makes $A/(\pi)=\mathcal O_{T_k,x}$ regular, and the nonzerodivisor dimension formula gives dimension one. Since $A$ is regular local of dimension two, $\pi$ cannot lie in $\mathfrak m^2$: otherwise the quotient would still have embedding dimension two. Thus $d=1$, even when $l/k$ is inseparable. If $l/k$ is inseparable, steps 2 and 6 give the claimed non-geometrically-reduced exceptional curve despite its coefficient being one.

source.place: Algebra Tags 00TF (lemma-flat-fibre-smooth), 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field), 00KW (lemma-one-equation), 00FP (lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation); embedding dimension definition of regularity.

proof.text:
For the separable smooth case use the smooth-point etale immersion slice $Z\hookrightarrow T$, with $Z_k$ consisting of $x$ and $\kappa(x)=l$. Locally this is a closed immersion, and $Z\to S$ is etale. On $T\times_S Z\to Z$ it gives a section; restrict to affine neighbourhoods to make this a closed section. The centred smooth-section coordinate theorem gives an etale coordinate $t$ carrying that section to zero. At its point over $x$ the pulled-back reduced point ideal is $(\pi',t)$: the diagonal factor of $l\otimes_kl$ is $l$, an open and closed factor since $l/k$ is finite separable, and other factors can be removed near this point. The projection from $T\times_S Z$ to $T$ and the coordinate map to $\mathbf A^1_Z$ are etale there. The closed fibre of the slice is reduced because it is etale over $k$, and its immersion identifies its residue field with $l$. Put $R'=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ at the special point of the slice and let $\pi'$ be the image of $\pi$; step 8 makes $R'$ a DVR. Localize the affine section-coordinate neighbourhoods at $z$; this leaves their special-fibre charts unchanged. Flat base change of the blowup then gives the following two model charts, with etale maps from the corresponding actual charts:
$$\operatorname{Spec}R'[v],\quad t=\pi'v;\qquad\operatorname{Spec}R'[t,w]/(tw-\pi').$$
These are the regular-sequence chart presentations for $(\pi',t)$ and $(t,\pi')$.

The first chart in step 11 is smooth over $R'$. The second is the $n=1$ nodal chart, hence has reduced nodal geometric fibres by the nodal-chart theorem. On its special fibre $tw=0$, the exceptional curve $t=0$ and the strict transform $w=0$ meet in one ordinary node; on the other chart the special fibre is a smooth affine line. To transport this to $T^+$, use the charts of step 11 before localizing at $z$: over an affine open $Z'\subseteq Z$ containing $z$, which is etale over $S$, they are $\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(Z',\mathcal O)[v]$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(Z',\mathcal O)[t,w]/(tw-\pi)$, again with etale maps from the corresponding actual charts. Both are flat and finitely presented over $S$. Since $Z'\to S$ is etale, each geometric fibre over $S$ is a disjoint union of copies of $\mathbf A^1_\Omega$, respectively of $\{tw=c\}$ with $c\in\Omega$. These are purely one-dimensional and smooth except at $t=w=0$ when $c=0$, where the completed local ring is $\Omega[[t,w]]/(tw)$. Apply the etale source-locality theorem for nodal families to a model chart with the family consisting of its identity and the etale map from the actual chart: each actual chart is nodal of relative dimension one over $S$. Apply it again on a neighbourhood of $E$ in $T^+$, to the family of these actual charts together with the open complement of $E$. The charts are etale over $T^+$ by base change, and their images cover $E$. Hence $T^+\to S$ is nodal of relative dimension one near $E$. Its geometric fibres there are reduced: they are smooth away from finitely many closed points, and at such a point the local ring injects into its completion $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$, which is reduced. Away from $E$, $q$ is an isomorphism, so after restricting to the original nodal neighbourhood these descriptions prove that $T^+\to S$ remains nodal near $E$. No connectedness of the family fibres is used.

source.place: Tag 0CDC (example-blowup), n=1 nodal model for the t-chart; Tag 0CDD (lemma-etale-local-at-worst-nodal), etale-local interpretation.

proof.text: For any geometric point of $T$ outside $x$ the fibre of $q$ is one point. For a geometric point over $x$, with algebraically closed field $\Omega$ over $l$, it is $E\times_l\Omega=\mathbf P^1_\Omega$. Its two standard affine charts have the dense generic point given by the zero ideal and have nonempty intersection $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega[t,t^{-1}]$; hence their union is irreducible, in particular nonempty and connected. This proves that all geometric fibres of $q$ are nonempty and connected, including in the inseparable case. The claim concerns $q$, not $T^+\to S$.

source.place: Tag 0AGQ (lemma-blowup), E is the projective line over the centre residue field; direct standard-chart connectedness check.

proof.text: Finally, on either chart near the exceptional curve its algebra is a subalgebra of the localization of the domain $A$, and the map $R\to A$ is injective. Thus it is torsion free as an $R$-module. The PID torsion-free flatness theorem makes each such chart flat over $R$; away from $E$ flatness is the assumed flatness of $T$. The finite-type composition theorem makes $T^+\to S$ finite type, since $q$ and $T\to S$ are finite type. Over the Noetherian ring $R$, every affine finite-type presentation is finite presentation. Moreover $T^+$ is Noetherian, hence quasi-separated, and the morphism is quasi-compact; these give finite presentation globally. If $T\to S$ is projective in the finite-projective-space convention, the projective-affine-base blowup theorem applies to its finite-type point ideal and proves projectivity of $T^+\to S$.

split_report.summary: Reuse existing regular-surface, regular-sequence, nodal-chart, strict-transform and field-tensor tools. Prove the exceptional coefficient by the initial form on a blowup chart, prove both defect-persistence assertions, and compute the smooth-centre charts. Clarify that nonempty connected geometric fibres belong to q, not the possibly disconnected family. No new nodes.
